newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian boy in race dispute gets U.S. visa.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian boy in race dispute gets U.S. visa.

text.p: A 6-year-old Brazilian boy at the centre of a dispute between Washington and Brasilia has been granted a U.S. visa, the American Embassy said on Friday.

A spokeswoman for the embassy in Brasilia said Carlos Alexandre Carvalho Rossi, who newspapers said had been refused a visa for an English language course in Florida because he was black, had been cleared to enter the United States.

U.S. officials denied that racial discrimination played a role, saying Rossi's parents -- his father, a white tax official, and his mother, a black housewife -- had failed to provide sufficient documentation.

Allegations in the Brazilian media that the U.S. consulate in Rio de Janeiro rejected Rossi's visa application because of racism threatened to overshadow the visit to Brazil this week by U.S. black leader the Rev. Jesse Jackson.
Rossi was one of 15 students due to fly to the United States in January to attend an English course. The other students, all white, had no difficulty in obtaining visas.

O Globo newspaper said on Friday that another visa dispute had erupted between Washington and Brasilia after the U.S. Embassy declined to grant entry permits to three Justice Ministry officials. But the embassy spokeswoman said the report was wrong. "We cannot give out details of each case but the Globo report contains several errors," she said.

The paper said three aides to Justice Minister Nelson Jobim had planned to attend a seminar in the United States and that Jobim protested to the embassy when their visas were denied. The embassy spokeswoman said the men were low-level ministry functionaries who had requested visas for private trips, not connected to official business.
The Brazilian Foreign Ministry said it was looking into the case and could make no further comment.
